title: Compare host output with an independently compiled fmt oracle
problem: The legacy test harness can share assumptions with the implementation; expected bytes need an independent formatting implementation.
example: A standalone fmt process formats INT64_MIN; a separate ffmt process must produce the identical bytes.
design: Compile fmt only into host reference executables, and compile ffmt targets without fmt headers. Require a clean checkout at the exact oracle pin without modifying it, and record format.h/format.cc hashes. Begin with four baseline cases supported before engine migration.
tradeoffs: Separate reference and target compilation reduces shared assumptions but costs compile time. Dirty or differently pinned oracle checkouts fail visibly. Accelerator routes and later feature cases arrive in independent changes.
docs: The host differential runner compiles the pinned fmt oracle independently. The reference checkout must be clean, and exact format.h/format.cc hashes are retained; verification never changes the caller checkout. Feature fixture modules are introduced with implementations; every loaded fixture file receives a source hash.
